 Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [for short 'the Act'] has been filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 15.04.2013 passed by the First Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Hubballi in M.V.C. No.77/2010 [for short, 'the Tribunal']
2.

entities.text: First Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Hubballi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 05.10.2010 at about 11:30 p.m., the claimant boarded the bus at CBT to go to his house from market after completing his business.

When the said bus came near Nehrunagar water tank, he got down from the bus and while he was crossing the road, the taxi bearing registration No.KA-25/C-385 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from Gokul side towards Hubballi and dashed to the claimant.
Due to the said impact, the claimant fell down and sustained injuries all over his body and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:17977 accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending bus by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondents appeared through their counsel and the respondent No.2 filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by the impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.1,91,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the amount of Rs.1,71,500/- and directed the insurance company and the owner of the vehicle to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved by the same, the present appeal has been filed.
6. Sri.Mrutyunjaya S. Hallikeri, the learned counsel for the appellant - claimant contended that due to the accident, the claimant suffered grievous injuries.
He has examined the Dr.Sunil Jituri as PW3.

sentences.text: 2 In his evidence, he has deposed that the claimant has suffered 40 to 45% disability to left lower limb.
Due to the disability, he is unable to do his day today work and the Tribunal has not granted any compensation towards loss of future earning.
7. Secondly, the learned counsel contended that due to the accident, the claimant has suffered disability up to 40 to 45% and he was inpatient for a period of 16 days.
He has suffered lot of pain during the treatment and he has to suffer this disability and unhappiness throughout his life.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and sufferings, loss of amenities and other incidental expenses is on lower side and hence, he sought to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

8. Per contra, Sri.G.N.Raichur, learned counsel appearing for the insurance company has contended that even though the doctor has assessed the limb disability up to 40 to 45%, but due to the said disability, the claimant has not suffered any loss of earning.
He has examined his employer.
He has categorically stated that he has continued his service and he was paying the salary even during the laid up period.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly not granted any NC: 2024:KHC-D:17977 compensation for future loss of income.

He further contended that considering the evidence of the doctor and the injuries suffered by the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal for pain and sufferings, loss of amenities and other incidental expenses are just and reasonable.
Hence, the learned counsel sought for dismissal of the appeal.
9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.

10. It is not in dispute that the claimant has suffered injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 05.10.2010 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of taxi bearing registration No.KA-25/C-385.
Due to that accident, the claimant has suffered fracture of neck of femur left hip and four part fracture of upper end of left humerus.
He has examined the Dr.Sunil Jituri as PW3.

In his evidence, he has deposed that the claimant has suffered 40 to 45% disability to left lower limb and due to the said disability, the claimant has not suffered any loss of earning, he has continued in his service.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly not awarded any compensation for future loss of income.
Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered NC: 2024:KHC-D:17977 grievous injuries.
He was inpatient for a period of 16 days.
He has suffered lots of pain during the treatment.
He has to suffer this disability and hardship throughout his life.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal for loss of amenities is on lower side and hence, I am inclined to enhance the same from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.1,00,000/-.
I am also inclined to enhance the amount towards future medical expenses from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
In respect of other heads are concerned, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

11. Thus, the claimant is entitled to the enhanced compensation as follows:
Compensation

Towards medical Rs.86,500/-

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The judgment and award dated 15.04.2013 passed by the First Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Hubballi in M.V.C. No.77/2010 is modified.
iii. The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,86,500/-.
iv. The respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

The respondent Nos.1 and 2 are directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
However, the compensation awarded under the head 'future medical expenses' shall not carry any interest.
